scale_005:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare financial data for our upcoming board meeting. I use {{vendor}} as our startup banking platform. If you don't already have this, ask me for: (1) confirmation that {{vendor}} is the correct platform, (2) the reporting period the board wants covered (e.g., last quarter), and (3) any specific accounts or entities to include if we have multiple.

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}}'s API and:
1. Pull current account/cash balances across all our business accounts.
2. Retrieve balance history over the reporting period so we can show a trend line (e.g., cash position at start vs. end of period).
3. Pull the transaction list for the quarter (or specified period), and categorize/summarize it into a board-friendly view: total inflows, total outflows, top spending categories, and any notable one-off transactions.
4. If {{vendor}} exposes accounting data via its API, pull relevant summary figures (e.g., burn rate, runway estimate) to cross-check against the transaction data.

Compile the results into a clean, structured summary (table or bullet format) suitable for dropping into a board deck, including: ending cash balance, net burn for the period, runway estimate if calculable, and a short list of notable transactions or anomalies worth flagging to the board.

Done looks like: a single financial summary document or section with balances, period-over-period cash trend, transaction summary, and any flagged items — sourced entirely from {{vendor}} data, with no placeholders left unfilled.

Report back with the compiled summary, the reporting period used, and any data gaps (e.g., missing categories, accounts you couldn't access) so I can address them before the deck is finalized.

scale_005:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the revenue metrics section of our board deck. I use {{vendor}} as my payments/billing platform, connected via its API using my configured credentials — ask me for my {{vendor}} account/workspace identifier if you need it, plus the reporting period (e.g. current quarter and trailing 12 months) if I haven't specified it.

Please do the following:

1. Use the {{vendor}} analytics capability to query key revenue metrics for the requested period: MRR (and MRR growth), gross payment volume, and any other standard revenue metrics available.
2. Use the {{vendor}} reporting capability to generate financial report runs (balance, payouts, revenue recognition) as CSV for the same period.
3. Pull payout and balance-transaction data and reconcile each bank deposit to its underlying charges, so the numbers tie out to actual cash movement.
4. Produce an itemized breakdown showing which charges, fees, refunds, and chargebacks make up each payout, so finance can verify the reconciliation.
5. Summarize the results into a clean board-ready format: a table or short section with MRR, MRR growth %, gross volume, net revenue after fees/refunds/chargebacks, and payout totals for the period, plus a one-paragraph narrative highlighting trends (growth rate, notable spikes/dips, refund/chargeback rate).

Done looks like: you have pulled and reconciled the metrics above, generated the CSV report(s), and produced a summarized deck-ready section with the table and narrative, plus links or file references to the underlying CSVs for backup.

Report back with: the summarized metrics table, the narrative paragraph, confirmation that deposits were reconciled to charges, and where the generated CSV reports can be found. Flag any discrepancies or data gaps you encounter instead of guessing at numbers.

scale_005:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a board meeting deck. I need a Profit & Loss (P&L) report pulled from our {{vendor}} accounting system for inclusion in the financials section.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already clear:
- Which {{vendor}} company/organization account to use (if we have more than one)
- The reporting period(s) required (e.g., the most recent fiscal quarter, year-to-date, or a specific custom date range the board wants to review)
- Whether comparison periods are needed (e.g., prior quarter, prior year, or budget-vs-actual)
- The output format preferred (PDF, spreadsheet/CSV, or both)

Then, using our configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}} via its documented API and generate the P&L report for the specified period(s) and comparison(s). Pull the report in an open format (e.g., CSV or similar) so figures can be inspected or reused in the deck. If useful for cross-checking totals, also retrieve the underlying general ledger or trial balance data through the API.

Verify the report looks complete and internally consistent: revenue, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and net income/loss lines should all be present with no obvious gaps or zeroed-out categories that shouldn't be zero. Flag anything that looks off (e.g., missing categories, unusually large one-time entries) rather than silently including it.

When done, report back with: the period(s) covered, a summary of top-line figures (total revenue, total expenses, net income/loss), the file(s) or data exported and where they're saved, and any anomalies or discrepancies you noticed that I should review before this goes into the board deck.

Do not make any changes to the accounting records — this is a read-only reporting task.

scale_005:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare KPI and burn rate calculations for an upcoming board meeting deck. I'll provide (or please ask me for if missing): access to our accounting system (e.g., QuickBooks or Xero) and bank account data via configured credentials, our current cash balance, our latest monthly financial statements (P&L and balance sheet), and our current headcount/payroll figures. Also ask me for the specific KPIs our board tracks (e.g., MRR, ARR, churn rate, CAC, LTV, gross margin, active users, growth rate) if not already defined.

Using this information, please:
1. Calculate gross burn (total monthly cash outflow) and net burn (cash outflow minus revenue/cash inflow) for the most recent 1-3 months.
2. Calculate our runway (current cash balance divided by average net burn) in months.
3. Compile the core KPIs I specify, showing current period value, prior period value, and month-over-month or quarter-over-quarter change.
4. Organize all figures into a clean summary table suitable for pasting into a board deck, with clear labels and units.
5. Flag any figures that look anomalous (e.g., missing data, sudden spikes) for my review rather than guessing or estimating them.

Done looks like: a complete, accurate KPI and burn rate summary table with month-over-month comparisons, runway calculation, and clear notes on any data gaps or anomalies you found.

Report back with the summary table, the runway figure in months, a one-paragraph narrative summary of burn trend (improving/worsening and why), and a list of any data points you had to leave blank or flag for my confirmation before they go into the deck.

scale_005:n5.prompt:
You are helping me draft our board meeting deck in Google Slides. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: (a) the link to our existing board deck template or last quarter's deck in Google Slides (or confirm you should create a new one), (b) our financial figures/reports for the period (revenue, burn, runway, cash balance), (c) key metrics/KPIs to highlight, (d) product update notes or a changelog, (e) current hiring plan/headcount changes, (f) the specific asks or decisions we want from the board this meeting, and (g) the target meeting date.

2. Using Google Slides (via the Slides app/API with my configured credentials), create or duplicate the deck and build out these sections in order: Cover/Agenda, Financial Summary, Key Metrics, Product Updates, Hiring Plan, Asks/Decisions Needed, Appendix (if relevant). Reuse our existing template's layout, fonts, and branding if a prior deck is provided.

3. Populate each section with the data I provide, formatting numbers into simple tables or charts where useful, and keep slide text concise (bullet points, not paragraphs). Flag clearly on any slide where data is missing or I still need to supply information (e.g., "[NEED: Q3 churn number]").

4. Do not invent numbers, projections, or claims — only use what I supply or what's already in the source deck.

5. When done, share the Google Slides link with me and provide a short summary of: which sections are fully complete, which have placeholders needing my input, and any inconsistencies you noticed versus the prior deck (e.g., metric definitions changed). This is a draft for my review — do not send or share it with board members.

scale_005:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the 'Strategy and Asks' section of my board deck. I will author the actual strategic narrative and investor/board asks myself, but I need you to prepare everything around it so I can drop my content in quickly.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: my company domain, my current board deck file or template (Google Slides, PowerPoint, or Notion doc), and the current business priorities I want the section to cover (e.g. fundraising, hiring, partnerships, product direction) if I haven't already given them.
2. Build a clean slide/section template titled 'Strategy & Asks' with placeholder headers such as: Where We Are Today, Strategic Priorities (Next 2-3 Quarters), Key Risks/Decisions Needed, and Specific Asks of the Board (e.g. intros, hires, fundraising support, approvals).
3. Pull supporting metrics and context from the rest of the deck (financials, KPIs, hiring plan, product updates already compiled) and insert relevant callouts or data points into the template so I have evidence at hand when writing the narrative.
4. Draft placeholder prompts/questions under each header (e.g. 'What is the #1 strategic bet this quarter?', 'What specific ask do you have of each board member?') to help me structure my thinking, but do NOT invent or write the actual strategy text, asks, or decisions on my behalf.
5. Compile a short checklist confirming the section is ready for me to fill in: template built, supporting metrics linked, placeholder prompts inserted.

When finished, report back with: a link or file reference to the prepared section, a summary of what data/metrics were pulled in, and the checklist status. Then stop for human sign-off — I will write the actual strategy narrative and asks and review the final section before it's added to the board deck.

scale_005:n7.prompt:
You are helping me publish our compiled board meeting deck to our team's board room space in {{vendor}}, our project-management/workspace tool. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: my {{vendor}} workspace details, the board room parent page/location where this should live, and the finalized board deck content (financials, metrics, product updates, hiring plan, and asks) — pull the latest version from wherever we've been assembling it if you have access, otherwise ask me to paste or point you to it.

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}}'s public API and prepare (but do not finalize) a new page under our board room location. Structure the page clearly with sections for: Financials, Metrics, Product Updates, Hiring Plan, and Asks — using headings, and where relevant, embedded tables or dashboard-style summaries consistent with how {{vendor}} supports rollups/widgets for portfolio-style reporting. Include a short summary/agenda block at the top.

Draft the full page content and show me a preview (or a link to the unpublished/draft page if {{vendor}} supports draft states) so I can review formatting, section order, and accuracy before it goes live to the board room. List any assumptions you made about content placement or missing data.

Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, do not create the final page or share it with the board room audience yet — prepare everything (draft content, structure, target location) and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the draft content or link, the target location in {{vendor}} where it will be published, a summary of what's included in each section, and any open questions or missing inputs you need from me before I approve publishing.

scale_005:n8.prompt:
You are helping me send our board deck to my board members ahead of our upcoming board meeting. Use {{vendor}} through its documented API or connection, with your configured credentials.

First, ask me for anything you don't have:
- The final board deck file, or a link to it, and confirmation that it is the final version
- The board member list: names and email addresses, plus anyone who should be Cc'd (observers, counsel) or Bcc'd
- The meeting date, time, location or video link, and any pre-read deadline
- Any specific asks or decisions I want the board to review in advance
- The inbox or address I want to send from

Then prepare the email in {{vendor}}:
1. Draft a concise message in my voice. Include a one-line purpose, the meeting logistics, a short bullet summary of what the deck covers (financials, key metrics, product updates, hiring plan, and asks), the specific decisions or input I need, and a request to send questions before the meeting.
2. Attach the deck, or include the link. Confirm the attachment opens and is the correct, final file.
3. Put the recipients in the correct To, Cc, and Bcc fields. Double-check that every address is spelled correctly and that no one outside the board list is included.
4. Save it as a draft. Do not send it.

Stop for human sign-off. Show me the full draft: subject, recipients by field, body, and attachment name and size. Then wait for my explicit approval. Apply any edits I request and show me the revised draft again. Send only after I clearly say to send. If {{vendor}} supports scheduled send or undo-send, tell me, and ask whether I want either option.

Done looks like this: after my approval, the email has been sent once to the approved recipients with the correct deck attached.

Report back with:
- The time the email was sent
- The final recipient list by field
- The subject line
- The message or thread ID from {{vendor}}
- Any bounces or delivery errors you can see
